Marco (Customer Success Manager): Hey team — just got a message from Sofia at AcmeHealth complaining their assistant started refusing routine triage prompts after yesterday's model rollout. She says it used to answer basic symptom-check flows and now returns a refusal ~60% of the time. Can anyone look?
Sofia (Customer): Yep — reproducer below. We send a short clinical-screener prompt and used to get a structured next-step recommendation. Now we get: 'I'm sorry, I can't help with that.' No change on our side. Example: prompt -> 'Patient reports mild cough and fever for 24 hours, no difficulty breathing. Suggest next steps.' Response -> refusal. This started ~2026-03-13 18:12 UTC after the automatic canary.
Jon (Support): Thanks Sofia — can you paste the full API request id or a convo snippet? Also which model id were you pinned to or using via the API?
Sofia (Customer): Request-id: req_0a9f3c2b. Using model: redwood-rlhf-clinic-2026-03 (not pinned; default routing). We didn't change prompts or rate limits.
Marco (Customer Success Manager): Jon — can you fetch logs for that request-id? Priya / Liam — heads up this might be an alignment/safety tweak.
Jon (Support): Pulling logs now. Found the request in gateway logs. Tokens: 87 prompt / 42 response max. Latency was 340ms. Model returned 200 with an output that starts with refusal text. Attaching anonymized transcript to thread.
Priya (ML Eng): Thanks — quick hypothesis: we pushed a safety-calibration update to the default RLHF variant during the canary on 2026-03-13 17:50 UTC. Canary went wide at ~18:05 UTC. The update tightened refusal heuristics for medical content to reduce under-refusal. It looks like AcmeHealth's use-case falls into a gray zone and is now being over-blocked.
Liam (SRE): DeployBot shows rollout job deploy-rlhf-safety-030 to default pool at 2026-03-13T17:47:23Z. Canary threshold passed automatically at 18:02. No infra errors.
Marco (Customer Success Manager): Ok — reproduce plan: Priya, can you confirm with a local instance whether the new safety profile rejects the sample? If so, can we quickly produce a temporary fallback mapping to the previous profile for this tenant?
Priya (ML Eng): Reproduced locally with model variant redwood-rlhf-clinic-2026-03@safety-v2 — same refusal. With safety-v1 (previous), it returns structured guidance. Quick mitigation options: 1) route AcmeHealth to safety-v1 model variant (fast, per-tenant routing), 2) relax safety calibration for the default pool (riskier), 3) ship a targeted prompt-safety override shim (per-customer plugin). I recommend 1 for immediate rollback.
Jon (Support): Marco — requested customer consent to route them to safety-v1 for 24-48h while we investigate. Sofia: okay to switch to that temporarily?
Sofia (Customer): Yes please — we're blocked on this flow for our triage pipeline. We prefer a temporary routing change while you fix the root cause.
Marco (Customer Success Manager): Implementing routing change now. @DeployBot can you set route override for tenant acmehealth -> redwood-rlhf-clinic-2026-03@safety-v1?
DeployBot: Route override created: tenant=acmehealth target=redwood-rlhf-clinic-2026-03@safety-v1 expires=2026-03-15T18:00:00Z by=marco_cs. :white_check_mark:
Liam (SRE): Verified traffic to safety-v1 nodes for tenant acmehealth. No capacity issues.
Sofia (Customer): Confirmed — triage flow back to normal. Thank you.
Priya (ML Eng): Next steps for root cause: I'll run a differential eval across our prompt set (safety, clinical triage, legal) to quantify false-positive increase post-safety-v2. Need prod logs for a random sample of refusals to compute false-positive rate. Jon — can you export 200 anonymized refusal examples from 2026-03-13 18:00 to 2026-03-14 03:00 for analysis? Include request_id, model_variant, prompt hash, and full model output.
Jon (Support): On it. Will sanitize and share an encrypted bucket link when ready.
Marco (Customer Success Manager): We should also notify Product that safety tuning caused customer-facing regressions for a high-impact vertical. Priya, can you estimate ETA to produce a fix or calibration tweak?
Priya (ML Eng): If we can get the 200 examples, I can run a model-in-the-loop classifier recalibration and produce a candidate safety-v2.1 within 48 hours. If that doesn't meet metrics, fallback to a narrower param change in 24h.
Marco (Customer Success Manager): Good. Sofia — we'll keep you updated; routing override stays in place until we validate a new profile. Any other customers seeing similar patterns?
Jon (Support): Searching support queue... flagged two more customers in health vertical reporting similar over-refusal since 3/13. I'll open separate threads but will correlate with Priya's dataset.
Sofia (Customer): Appreciate the quick response. One note: we sometimes call the API via a batching proxy — could batching affect the classifier decisions? We observed varying behavior across single vs batched requests.
Priya (ML Eng): Good catch — safety hooks run per-request. Batching merges prompts; if we see combined context it can increase conservatism. Include an example of a batched request in the export.
Liam (SRE): FYI infra note: routing overrides add small policy checks but latency remains within SLO. No billing implications for temporary routing.
Marco (Customer Success Manager): Action items: Jon export anonymized refusals -> Priya; Priya run recalibration + candidate -> QA; Marco/Support keep customer updated and maintain routing override. Leaving thread open until we deploy a validated fix. :eyes:
